name: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023

chapters.title: Limited partnerships, register of overseas entities (Parts 2–3)
Corporate criminal liability — identification principle (Part 5, s.196)
Failure to prevent fraud (Part 5, ss.199-206 + Sched 13)

articles.title: Identification principle for economic crime
articles.requirement: A body corporate is treated as committing a listed economic-crime offence if a senior manager, acting within the actual or apparent scope of their authority, commits the offence. Replaces the narrow common-law 'directing mind and will' test for the listed offences (fraud, false accounting, theft, tax offences, sanctions, money laundering, bribery, etc.) — in force 26 Dec 2023; expanded to all economic crimes 1 Sept 2025.

articles.title: Failure to prevent fraud
articles.requirement: A 'large' relevant body (s.201 threshold) commits an offence if a person associated with it commits a base fraud offence (Sched 13) intending to benefit the body or its clients. Strict liability subject to the s.199(4) reasonable-procedures defence. Triable on indictment; unlimited fine. In force 1 Sept 2025.

articles.title: Reasonable procedures defence
articles.requirement: It is a defence for the body to prove that at the time of the base offence it had in place such fraud-prevention procedures as it was reasonable in all the circumstances to expect it to have had, OR that it was not reasonable in all the circumstances to expect it to have any procedures. The Home Office statutory guidance (Nov 2024) sets out six principles informing this assessment.

articles.title: Associated person — definition
articles.requirement: A person is associated with the body if they are (a) an employee, agent or subsidiary, or (b) a person who otherwise performs services for or on behalf of the body. Captures contractors, intermediaries, joint-venture partners — not arm's-length suppliers.

articles.title: Large organisation threshold
articles.requirement: An organisation is 'large' if in the financial year preceding the alleged offence it satisfied two or more of: (a) turnover > £36 million, (b) balance sheet total > £18 million, (c) more than 250 employees. Applied at parent level for groups; subsidiaries inherit parent's status.

articles.title: Base offence — Fraud by false representation (FA 2006 s.2)
articles.requirement: Dishonestly making a false representation, intending to make a gain for self/another or to cause loss to another or expose to risk of loss.

articles.title: Base offence — Fraud by failing to disclose (FA 2006 s.3)
articles.requirement: Dishonestly failing to disclose information which the defendant is under a legal duty to disclose, with the requisite intent to gain or cause loss.

articles.title: Base offence — Fraud by abuse of position (FA 2006 s.4)
articles.requirement: Dishonestly abusing a position in which the defendant is expected to safeguard the financial interests of another.

articles.title: Base offence — Obtaining services dishonestly (FA 2006 s.11)
articles.requirement: Obtaining services by a dishonest act, intending payment to be avoided.

articles.title: Base offence — False accounting (Theft Act 1968 s.17)
articles.requirement: Dishonestly destroying, defacing, concealing or falsifying any account or document made for an accounting purpose.

articles.title: Base offence — Fraudulent trading (Companies Act 2006 s.993)
articles.requirement: Carrying on the business of a company with intent to defraud creditors, or for any fraudulent purpose.

articles.title: Base offence — Cheating the public revenue (common law)
articles.requirement: Common-law offence of fraudulent conduct designed to prejudice the public revenue.

articles.title: Principle 1 — Top-level commitment
articles.requirement: The organisation's top-level management (board, executive directors) is committed to preventing fraud by associated persons. They demonstrate this through clear, written commitment communicated internally and externally; provide governance and resources; ensure the organisation has a culture in which fraud is unacceptable.

articles.title: Principle 2 — Risk assessment
articles.requirement: The organisation assesses the nature and extent of its exposure to the risk of associated persons committing the Sched 13 fraud offences for the benefit of the organisation. The assessment is documented, kept up to date, refreshed on material change (new business line, M&A, regulatory change), and informed by sector / geography / customer / product / transaction risk factors.

articles.title: Principle 3 — Proportionate risk-based prevention procedures
articles.requirement: The organisation's fraud-prevention procedures are proportionate to the risks it faces. Each identified fraud risk has at least one targeted control. Procedures are clear, practical, accessible to those who need them, effectively implemented and enforced. Includes financial controls (segregation of duties, approval thresholds, four-eyes review), system-level controls, and sector-specific controls.

articles.title: Principle 4 — Due diligence
articles.requirement: The organisation applies due diligence procedures to associated persons proportionate to the fraud risk. Includes employee pre-hire screening, due diligence on agents / intermediaries / JV partners before engagement, periodic refresh, and event-driven re-assessment.

articles.title: Principle 5 — Communication (including training)
articles.requirement: Anti-fraud policies are embedded through communication and training. Internal: mandatory training appropriate to risk and role, refreshed periodically, completion tracked. External: anti-fraud expectations communicated to associated persons via contracts, codes of conduct, joint training, supplier handbooks.

articles.title: Principle 6 — Monitoring and review
articles.requirement: The organisation monitors the effectiveness of its fraud-prevention procedures and reviews them periodically. Includes KPIs / metrics, internal audit coverage, incident learning loop (post-incident review feeding back into procedure design), whistleblower channels, and external assurance where proportionate.
